hyps.why: Replacing a removed direct edge with a 3x3 conv adds a whole new path and gains far more than replacing an existing operation.
Turning a missing edge into a conv adds a new path to node 2, which beats swapping one existing op for another.
Adding a residual shortcut where there was none helps much more than replacing a conv with a skip, which can hurt.
With edge 0 removed, node 1 receives no input, so a conv on edge 4 is dead.
Edge 2 starts at node 1, which is disconnected from the input when edge 0 is none.
Removing an existing 3x3 conv loses accuracy, whereas setting none on an edge that is already none changes nothing.
When another strong path into the output already exists, an extra 3x3 conv on the direct edge adds less.
Reconnecting the input to node 1 activates paths through edges 2 and 4, a bigger gain than upgrading an existing op.
Restoring the edge into the output node adds a path from node 2, a larger gain than replacing a weaker op.
Without edge 1, node 2 depends only on the node 1 path, so a conv on edge 5 is less useful.
